elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare. We aimed to enhance our understanding of sustainability definitions, research designs, data collection methods, timing, measures, and sustainability outcomes used for sustainability evaluation studies.
elements.reason: Objectives are explicitly stated in a dedicated Aim section, also echoed in the abstract.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare.
elements.reason: This is an integrative review of approaches to evaluating sustainability, not a review of intervention effects, so PICO-style planned comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal • Were primary research • Had explicit research design and data collection methods • Had an explicit theoretical approach for sustainability ... • Were within a healthcare setting • Evaluated the sustainability of an EBI
elements.reason: Table 1 specifies study characteristics for eligibility, including study design (primary research with explicit design), healthcare setting (with a detailed definition of healthcare settings), and the requirement of an explicit theoretical approach and independent sustainability evaluation component.

elements.quote: • Were published in a peer-review journal ... Exclusion criteria: • Were gray literature
elements.reason: Publication status (peer-reviewed, no gray literature) is specified, but dissemination year and language restrictions are not stated in the eligibility criteria; the English-language restriction appears only in the Limitations section (text_21), not as an explicit eligibility criterion.

elements.quote: Did not evaluate the sustainability of an EBI or QI intervention using a defined approach
elements.reason: Exclusion was based on whether sustainability was evaluated using a defined approach, not on outcome measurement or reporting; the distinction between outcomes not measured versus not reported does not apply to this review's eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: The two reviewers independently extracted the following variables: (1) study design, (2) evaluation type (independent versus composite), (3) sustainability definition and terms used, (4) type and name of theoretical approach, (5) purpose of approach use ...
elements.reason: Data extraction variables suggest grouping dimensions (e.g., evaluation type, type of theoretical approach), but the groups used in each synthesis are not explicitly specified or linked to the review objectives' comparisons.
No rationale is provided for notable restrictions such as excluding gray literature, requiring an independent sustainability evaluation component, or restricting to healthcare settings.
